messages.content: Please reprice both nonstop round trips for November 28 through December 4. I want the full schedules against six hotel nights, plus baggage and change terms. The resort quotes now have different expiration dates, so we need to settle the flights.

For two adults in standard economy, I found two complete nonstops. Alaska is $1,012 total: depart SFO Saturday at 8:10 a.m., arrive PVR at 1:02 p.m.; return Friday at 2:20 p.m., arrive SFO at 4:38 p.m. United is $1,086 total: depart at 10:45 a.m., arrive at 3:37 p.m.; return at 4:55 p.m., arrive at 7:14 p.m. Both fares are available now, subject to repricing before ticketing.
Put the 8:10 option first. I prefer morning departures when there is no trip-specific reason to leave later. How do those arrival times work with check-in?

Alaska aligns better. After immigration, bags, and the reserved transfer, the estimated resort arrival is 2:15-2:45 p.m., close to the 3:00 p.m. check-in at either property. United would put you at the resort around 4:50-5:20 p.m., using less of the first afternoon. Both itineraries cover the same six nights, November 28 through December 4.
And the returns relative to checkout? I do not want to spend half a day waiting at the airport, but I also do not want a rushed transfer.

Both resorts have noon checkout. For Alaska, a 12:10 p.m. pickup is appropriate for the 2:20 p.m. flight, so you could check out at noon and leave directly. For United, pickup would be about 2:40 p.m.; you would need luggage storage and roughly two and a half hours at the property after checkout. Late checkout is not included in either current room quote.
Alaska is clearly the better schedule. Before we buy it, compare exactly what the two economy fares include.

The $1,012 Alaska Main fare includes seat selection at booking, one carry-on and one personal item per traveler. Checked bags are $35 for the first bag each way per traveler, or $140 total if each of you checks one bag round trip. Changes are permitted without an airline change fee, but any fare difference applies; cancellation produces future travel credit rather than a cash refund. The $1,086 United Economy fare also includes advance seat selection, one carry-on and one personal item. First checked bags are $40 each way, or $160 total for the same baggage plan. It likewise has no change fee, with fare differences due, and cancellation yields future flight credit.
So Alaska is $1,152 with one checked bag each, versus $1,246 on United?

Correct. Those totals include the currently quoted airfare and one standard checked bag per person in each direction. They do not include optional preferred seats, onboard purchases, or any later fare increase before ticketing.
Can Alaska be held, and how does the timing compare with the resort deadlines?

Alaska offers a complimentary 24-hour hold on this itinerary. The flexible beachfront room rate expires tomorrow at 6:00 p.m. Pacific, while the adults-only spa resort quote expires two days later at 6:00 p.m. Pacific. A hold would protect the flight price through tomorrow at 3:40 p.m. Pacific, leaving only a short interval to finalize the beachfront property.

That is too tight, and the schedule works for either resort. Purchase the Alaska Main itinerary for both of us. Add one checked bag each in both directions, use the traveler details already on file, and leave the resorts unbooked.

Before ticketing: the total charge is $1,152 for two Alaska Main round trips and four one-way checked-bag fees. The tickets are nonrefundable to the original payment method after the 24-hour cancellation window; later voluntary cancellation returns eligible value as airline credit, and changes may require a fare difference. Shall I charge the card ending in 1842?

Purchased. The card ending in 1842 was charged $1,152. Your itinerary is SFO-PVR on Saturday, November 28, departing 8:10 a.m. and arriving 1:02 p.m.; PVR-SFO on Friday, December 4, departing 2:20 p.m. and arriving 4:38 p.m. One checked bag per traveler is included each way, and the airline confirmation is K7M4QX. The flexible beachfront and adults-only spa resorts remain unbooked; their quoted rates expire tomorrow and the following day, respectively.
